Operator:
Good day and thank you for standing by. Welcome to the GlobalTech Solutions Q3 Earnings Conference Call. At this time, all participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a Q&A session. Today’s call is being recorded.
I would now like to hand the call over to Janet Barnes, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Janet Barnes, VP of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to GlobalTech Solutions’ Q3 earnings call. With me today are Alex Johnson, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; David Lee, COO; and Emily Carter, CTO.
Earlier today, we published our press release and earnings slides, which are available on our IR website. Please note that this call may contain forward-looking statements. With that, I’ll turn it over to Alex Johnson.

Alex Johnson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thanks, Janet, and welcome, everyone.

We had a strong quarter with performance driven by several key initiatives. First, I’d like to address our operating margin performance. While specific company-wide operating margin numbers aren't provided in the summary, we can infer a slight overall contraction based on the mixed performance of the individual business units. Let's assume, for the sake of this analysis, that the company's overall operating margin landed at 28.5% in Q4, compared to 29.2% in Q3 and 29.5% in Q4 of the prior year. This suggests a downward trend, albeit a manageable one. In our Client Computing Group, operating profit likely experienced a slight dip sequentially. Let's say CCG's Q3 operating profit was around $4.8 billion, translating to an operating margin of approximately 35%. In Q4, with increased spending, the operating profit might have decreased to $4.7 billion, bringing the operating margin down to roughly 34%. This decline is attributable to the increased investments in R&D, specifically targeting next-generation CPU architectures (e.g., "Lunar Lake" development) and advanced graphics solutions to compete more effectively. The reported 3% year-over-year decrease in CCG operating profit is significant. Last year, CCG operating profit might have been $4.85 billion. This year, it is $4.7 billion. This decline is primarily due to a confluence of factors. Firstly, while unit sales in the premium notebook segment remained strong (a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion), ASPs (Average Selling Prices) were under pressure due to increased competition and promotional activities to clear existing inventory of older-generation chips. Secondly, R&D spending increased by approximately 8% year-over-year to $1.8 billion, reflecting the aggressive investment in future product generations. Finally, increased marketing spend to drive adoption of new features like integrated AI capabilities in new CPUs also contributed to the decline. This decrease was partially offset by reduced manufacturing costs due to efficiency improvements in the production of existing CPU architectures, which reduced COGS (Cost of Goods Sold) by roughly 2%. Let's assume that last quarter's guidance projected a CCG operating margin of 35.5%. The actual result of 34% fell short by 1.5 percentage points. The primary reason for this deviation was likely underestimated costs associated with the accelerated development of the "Meteor Lake" CPU family, particularly the integration of the tile-based architecture and the increased complexity of the manufacturing process. Supply chain challenges, specifically the availability of certain key components from TSMC, also caused inefficiencies and increased costs. In our Data Center Group, DCG likely experienced a more pronounced sequential decline in operating margin. The one-time GlobalTech Federal-related charge significantly impacted profitability. If DCG's Q3 operating profit was approximately $3.2 billion (an operating margin of, say, 25%), the Q4 profit might have dropped to $2.65 billion (roughly 20.5% operating margin) after accounting for the federal charge and the 7nm product ramp. The 17% year-over-year decrease in operating profit is substantial. Assuming a prior-year operating profit of $3.2 billion, the current operating profit stands at $2.65 billion. The "one-time GlobalTech Federal-related charge" could stem from a project termination or renegotiation leading to a significant write-down. The 7-nanometer product ramp is also a key factor. While 7nm product revenue increased by 45% year-over-year to $1.8 billion, the initial production costs of the 7nm process are significantly higher than those of the previous generation (14nm). This is due to lower yields and the increased complexity of the manufacturing process. The increased mix of 7nm products within the overall DCG revenue mix put further pressure on operating margins. Suppose the guidance for DCG operating margin last quarter was 24%. The actual result of 20.5% significantly missed the mark, by 3.5 percentage points. This substantial deviation was likely driven by an underestimation of both the size of the GlobalTech Federal-related charge (which could have been related to project delays or cancellations) and the ramp costs associated with the 7nm process, especially given the challenges in achieving optimal yields. Furthermore, increased competition put pressure on ASPs, further impacting profitability. The full-year operating profit being down due to lower revenue, increased mix of 7nm products, GlobalTech 4 start-up charges, and increased investment in the product roadmap underscores the company's ongoing transition. The GlobalTech 4 start-up costs specifically refer to the initial expenses related to setting up and optimizing the production of chips based on the GlobalTech 4 process node. These costs include equipment depreciation, facility expenses, and employee training.

We also made meaningful progress with our revenue results this quarter. Q4 2021 delivered a resounding performance, exceeding initial revenue guidance by a significant margin. Reported revenue for the quarter reached $19.5 billion, surpassing the previous guidance of $18.3 billion by $1.2 billion (a 6.5% outperformance). This strong finish contributed to a full-year 2021 revenue of $74.7 billion, $1.2 billion above the initially projected $73.5 billion. While the full year saw a modest 2% year-over-year growth, the underlying drivers suggest a strong foundation for continued expansion in key segments. The $19.5 billion in Q4 revenue represents a notable achievement, particularly considering the ongoing supply chain constraints and global economic uncertainties. The outperformance relative to guidance was primarily driven by three key factors: Strong Enterprise and Government Data Center Demand: Revenue from the Data Center Solutions Group (DCSG) reached $7.8 billion in Q4, a 9% increase quarter-over-quarter and a substantial 15% increase year-over-year. This surge was fueled by increased adoption of our next-generation "Everest" server platform, particularly within the government sector, where we secured several large contracts related to national infrastructure modernization projects. Specifically, we saw a 22% increase in sales to federal government agencies compared to Q3. Within the enterprise segment, the accelerated transition to hybrid cloud environments and the growing demand for AI and machine learning workloads boosted demand for high-performance computing (HPC) solutions, contributing approximately $650 million to DCSG revenue. Resilient Desktop PC Performance: Despite earlier concerns about a slowdown in the desktop PC market, Q4 witnessed a surprising resurgence. Desktop PC revenue reached $4.5 billion, exceeding our internal projections by approximately $300 million. This resilience can be attributed to several factors: Continued Demand from Commercial Sector: Businesses are continuing to upgrade their desktop infrastructure to support hybrid work models, requiring more powerful and secure machines. Our new "Titan" series desktop, featuring enhanced security features and remote management capabilities, has been particularly well-received. Gaming Market Strength: The high-end gaming market remains robust, with demand for our "Apex" gaming desktops exceeding expectations. We saw a 12% increase in Apex sales compared to Q3, driven by the launch of new graphics cards and a compelling software bundle. Better-than-Expected Notebook Demand: Notebook revenue reached $5.2 billion in Q4, outperforming our guidance by approximately $400 million. This positive surprise was driven by: Education Sector Purchases: Many educational institutions accelerated their technology refresh cycles in Q4, investing in new notebooks for students and faculty. Our "Scholar" series notebook, specifically designed for the education market, experienced a 25% increase in sales quarter-over-quarter. Strong Holiday Season Sales: The holiday season saw a significant increase in consumer demand for notebooks, particularly in the mid-range segment. Our promotional campaigns and attractive financing options helped drive sales. Overall, Q4 revenue increased by 7% compared to Q3 2021 ($18.2 billion). This growth was primarily driven by the aforementioned factors, with DCSG and Notebook showing the most significant gains. The $19.5 billion in Q4 2021 represents a 5% increase compared to Q4 2020 ($18.6 billion). The year-over-year growth rate has accelerated compared to the previous quarters, reflecting the positive impact of our strategic initiatives and market trends. The full-year revenue of $74.7 billion represents a 2% increase compared to 2020 ($73.2 billion). While the growth rate is relatively modest, it is important to note the significant headwinds faced during the year, including: Supply Chain Disruptions: Global chip shortages and logistical bottlenecks significantly impacted our ability to meet demand for certain products, particularly in the first half of the year. We estimate that supply chain constraints reduced our full-year revenue by approximately $1.5 billion. Currency Fluctuations: Unfavorable currency exchange rates, particularly in emerging markets, negatively impacted our revenue by approximately $500 million. Despite these challenges, we were able to achieve growth through: Strategic Investments in R&D: Our ongoing investments in research and development have enabled us to launch innovative products and solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. Expansion into New Markets: We have expanded our presence in key growth markets, such as cloud computing and artificial intelligence, positioning us for long-term success. Enhanced Customer Relationships: We have strengthened our relationships with key customers, enabling us to secure large contracts and drive repeat business. As previously mentioned, Q4 revenue exceeded guidance by $1.2 billion, and full-year revenue exceeded guidance by $1.2 billion. The key reasons for this outperformance include: Underestimation of Enterprise and Government Demand: Our initial guidance underestimated the strength of demand from the enterprise and government sectors, particularly for data center solutions. Conservative Desktop PC Forecast: We had initially anticipated a more significant decline in the desktop PC market, but the market proved to be more resilient than expected. Effective Promotional Campaigns: Our promotional campaigns during the holiday season were highly effective in driving sales of notebooks and other consumer products.

On a broader level, our fab construction progress supported our positioning this quarter. This report details the significant progress made in the construction of GlobalTech's two new fabrication facilities (fabs), Fab 53 and Fab 54, located in Chandler, Arizona, during the third quarter of 2024. As previously communicated, the groundbreaking ceremony for both fabs occurred in late June, three months ahead of the initially projected schedule outlined in the Q4 2023 capital expenditure plan. This accelerated timeline is a testament to meticulous pre-planning, strong collaboration with local authorities, and proactive supply chain management. The early groundbreaking has a ripple effect across the entire project timeline. We now anticipate initial tool move-in for Fab 53 to commence in Q2 2025, approximately two months ahead of the original schedule. For Fab 54, we project tool move-in to begin in Q4 2025, maintaining its accelerated pace. This early start is crucial for achieving our stated goal of significantly increasing domestic chip production capacity by 2027. As of the end of Q3, both Fab 53 and Fab 54 have completed foundation work. This involved the pouring of over 1.2 million cubic yards of concrete, a monumental task requiring precise coordination and logistics. Currently, structural steel erection is approximately 65% complete for Fab 53 and 50% complete for Fab 54. We are closely monitoring the global steel market and have secured fixed-price contracts with key suppliers to mitigate potential cost volatility. We've also implemented a "just-in-time" delivery system for steel components to minimize on-site storage and optimize construction flow. A significant portion of Q3 has been dedicated to the preliminary design and engineering of the advanced cleanroom infrastructure for both fabs. These facilities will adhere to the highest cleanroom standards (ISO Class 3 or better) to ensure minimal particle contamination during chip manufacturing. We are partnering with leading cleanroom technology providers, including XYZ CleanTech and ABC Solutions, to implement state-of-the-art air filtration systems, automated material handling, and advanced monitoring equipment. The initial investment in cleanroom technology for both fabs is projected to exceed $750 million. Alongside the fab structure itself, concurrent progress is being made on critical infrastructure development. This includes the construction of a dedicated power substation to supply the substantial electricity demands of the new facilities. The substation is projected to have a capacity of 500 MW, sufficient to power both fabs at full operational capacity. Additionally, we are investing heavily in water purification and recycling systems to minimize our environmental footprint. We aim to recycle at least 80% of the water used in the manufacturing process. Furthermore, the project includes extensive gas and chemical delivery systems, which are being designed with enhanced safety and redundancy measures. The Arizona fab expansion is already having a positive impact on the local economy. Construction activities have generated approximately 8,000 construction jobs in Q3, and we anticipate this number to peak at over 12,000 in Q1 2025. Furthermore, once operational, Fab 53 and Fab 54 are expected to create over 3,000 high-skilled permanent jobs in areas such as engineering, manufacturing, and research. We are actively collaborating with local universities and community colleges to develop training programs to ensure a pipeline of qualified talent. We've also seen a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion in the Semiconductor Manufacturing Equipment sector due to increased orders related to GlobalTech's fab expansion. Given the ongoing global supply chain challenges, we have implemented a comprehensive risk mitigation strategy. This includes diversifying our supplier base, increasing inventory levels of critical components, and proactively identifying potential bottlenecks. We are also leveraging advanced analytics and artificial intelligence to optimize our supply chain and improve forecasting accuracy. We have secured long-term contracts for critical materials like neon gas and polysilicon, mitigating the impact of potential supply disruptions. The accelerated construction timeline and advanced technology investments have resulted in a slight increase in our capital expenditure guidance for FY24. We now project total capital expenditures to be in the range of $28 billion to $30 billion, up from the previous guidance of $27 billion to $29 billion. However, we believe that this increased investment is justified by the long-term strategic benefits of expanding our domestic manufacturing capacity and reducing our reliance on overseas suppliers. We expect these fabs to be instrumental in achieving a 20% reduction in manufacturing costs per chip by 2028, driven by improved efficiency and economies of scale.

I’ll now hand it over to Sarah Chen to walk you through the financials.

Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Alex, and hello, everyone.

This quarter’s financial results were underpinned by operational rigor and discipline. Let’s walk through the key metrics.

To start, government grants, local grants, tax incentives, and loans helped drive improvements. As GlobalTech management has stated, the progress of the CHIPS Act in both the US and EU represents a significant catalyst for their ambitious investment plans. We're not just talking about feel-good legislation; we're talking about tangible financial levers that are fundamentally altering GlobalTech's capital expenditure calculus. The core of the US CHIPS Act is the direct provision of grants to semiconductor manufacturers. While the exact allocation to GlobalTech remains fluid and dependent on project specifics, our analysis indicates that GlobalTech is aggressively pursuing funding for several key initiatives. The Arizona Expansion of Fab 53 & Fab 62, already under construction, are prime candidates for CHIPS Act funding. We project that GlobalTech could secure grants covering between 15-25% of the total construction costs of these fabs. Assuming a combined cost of approximately $20 billion for the two fabs, this translates to potential grant funding in the range of $3 billion to $5 billion. The timing of these grants is crucial. We anticipate initial tranches of funding to be released in late 2024, with subsequent installments tied to specific construction milestones and job creation targets. This funding will be instrumental in mitigating GlobalTech's short-term capital expenditure burden and improving their overall return on invested capital (ROIC) on these projects. The proposed mega-site in Ohio represents a long-term strategic bet for GlobalTech. The scale of this project, potentially reaching $100 billion over a decade, necessitates substantial government support. We believe GlobalTech will leverage the CHIPS Act to secure a significant portion of the funding. Our projections indicate that GlobalTech could receive grant funding covering up to 30% of the initial phase of the Ohio project, potentially translating to $9 billion in upfront funding. However, these grants are likely to be contingent on GlobalTech meeting stringent requirements regarding workforce development, domestic sourcing, and technology transfer. A key component of the CHIPS Act is support for advanced packaging technologies. GlobalTech is investing heavily in this area, particularly at its facilities in New Mexico and Oregon. We estimate that GlobalTech could secure grants covering 10-15% of the capital expenditure associated with these advanced packaging expansions, potentially totaling $500 million to $750 million. Beyond the federal CHIPS Act, GlobalTech is actively pursuing local grants and incentives in the states where it is expanding its operations. The state of Arizona is highly incentivized to attract and retain semiconductor manufacturing. We anticipate that GlobalTech will receive significant property tax abatements, infrastructure improvements, and workforce training grants from the state and local governments. These incentives could collectively reduce GlobalTech's operating costs in Arizona by 5-8% over the next decade. We project a specific local grant of $100 million to be awarded in Q4 2024 for workforce development initiatives directly tied to the Arizona expansion. The state of Ohio is offering a comprehensive package of incentives to attract GlobalTech's mega-site. This includes tax credits, infrastructure grants, and workforce training programs. We estimate that these incentives could reduce GlobalTech's effective tax rate in Ohio by 3-5% over the next 15 years. We also anticipate significant infrastructure investments by the state, such as road improvements and utility upgrades, which will further reduce GlobalTech's capital expenditure burden. In 2023, GlobalTech's Rio Rancho, New Mexico facility saw a 15% increase in production output thanks to a $3.5 billion upgrade. The state has offered a tax credit of $12 million over the next five years, tied to maintaining specific employment levels and continuing to invest in the facility. This is a smaller-scale example, but it demonstrates the importance of local incentives in optimizing GlobalTech's cost structure. Tax incentives play a crucial role in reducing GlobalTech's tax burden and improving its profitability. The ITC allows companies to deduct a percentage of their investment in qualified property from their taxes. We anticipate that GlobalTech will utilize the ITC to reduce its tax liability associated with its investments in new fabs and equipment. The specifics of the ITC are ever-evolving, but currently, we estimate this could provide a tax credit of up to 7% on qualified investments. GlobalTech is a major investor in R&D, and it will continue to aggressively pursue the R&D tax credit. We estimate that this credit could reduce GlobalTech's tax liability by $500 million to $750 million annually. Furthermore, the CHIPS Act includes provisions to enhance the R&D tax credit for semiconductor manufacturers, which could further boost GlobalTech's tax savings. This quarter, GlobalTech expects a tax refund of approximately $250 million related to prior-year R&D tax credits and investment tax credits. This refund will provide a temporary boost to GlobalTech's cash flow and improve its short-term financial performance. Based on preliminary estimates, GlobalTech anticipates receiving a tax credit refund of approximately $300 million this quarter. This refund is primarily attributable to overpayments of estimated taxes and adjustments to prior-year R&D tax credits. The refund will positively impact GlobalTech's cash flow and net income for the quarter. While grants and tax incentives are preferred, loans also play a role in GlobalTech's financing strategy, particularly for larger projects. The US government, through agencies like the Department of Energy, may offer direct loans to support strategic investments in semiconductor manufacturing. We believe GlobalTech could pursue direct loans to finance a portion of its Ohio mega-site. These loans typically offer favorable interest rates and repayment terms, making them an attractive financing option. Loan guarantees reduce the risk for private lenders, making it easier for GlobalTech to secure financing at competitive rates. We anticipate that GlobalTech will explore the possibility of securing loan guarantees from government agencies to support its expansion plans. The EU CHIPS Act mirrors the US legislation, aiming to bolster semiconductor manufacturing within Europe. GlobalTech has significant operations in Europe, particularly in Ireland and Germany. GlobalTech is already a major employer in Ireland, and the EU CHIPS Act could incentivize further investment in its Irish facilities. We anticipate that GlobalTech will pursue grants and tax incentives under the EU CHIPS Act to expand its manufacturing capacity and develop new technologies in Ireland. GlobalTech has announced plans to build a major new fabrication facility in Magdeburg, Germany. This project is a prime candidate for funding under the EU CHIPS Act. We estimate that GlobalTech could secure grants covering up to 40% of the total construction costs of this fab, potentially totaling €6 billion to €8 billion. This funding will be crucial for making the Magdeburg project economically viable. Securing EU CHIPS Act funding requires GlobalTech to align its investment plans with the EU's strategic priorities, such as promoting technological sovereignty and strengthening the European semiconductor ecosystem. This may require GlobalTech to collaborate with other European companies and research institutions.

Additionally, our capital expenditure showed strong results. Q3 2024 saw a strategically planned increase in CapEx, driven by both ongoing infrastructure upgrades and investments in new technological initiatives aimed at boosting operational efficiency and expanding our market reach. While the overall CapEx spend increased by 22% compared to Q3 2023, the allocation reflects a shift towards software and digitalization efforts, positioning us for long-term sustainable growth. This quarter's CapEx spend totalled $115 million, compared to $94 million in Q3 2023. Building upon the 2021 baseline of roughly 60% equipment and 40% space build-out, we see a significant evolution in the composition of our CapEx investments. Equipment, at 45% of Q3 2024 CapEx, or $51.75 million, while still significant, has decreased as a percentage of overall CapEx. This is partially due to increased efficiency gains from existing equipment and a strategic shift towards cloud-based solutions, reducing the need for massive hardware purchases. A substantial portion of equipment spend ($28 million) was dedicated to upgrading manufacturing facilities in our Southeast Asian hubs (Vietnam and Malaysia). This investment is focused on implementing automated systems and robotics to increase production capacity by an estimated 18% by Q1 2025, thereby addressing the anticipated increased demand following a 15% increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion, largely attributed to our consumer electronics division. Specific upgrades included the installation of new Surface Mount Technology (SMT) lines and advanced testing equipment. Another $15 million was allocated to refreshing hardware within our North American data centers. This included upgrading servers to support the growing demands of our AI-powered customer service platform, implemented earlier this year, which has seen a 20% adoption rate among our user base. The upgrade includes implementing next-generation GPUs to better handle the computation of AI driven software. We invested $8.75 million in upgrading our logistics infrastructure, including the purchase of more fuel efficient and electric vehicles, to reduce our carbon footprint and improve delivery times. We are actively testing autonomous delivery solutions in select urban markets, and this CapEx includes the initial investment in necessary infrastructure for these pilot programs. Space build-out at 25% of Q3 2024 CapEx, or $28.75 million, has seen a moderate decrease in percentage from the 2021 baseline. A significant portion of this allocation ($18 million) was dedicated to expanding our Research and Development (R&D) facilities in Silicon Valley. This expansion is crucial for supporting our ongoing development of next-generation technologies, particularly in the areas of advanced materials and artificial intelligence. The build-out includes specialized labs with controlled environments and advanced testing equipment. The remaining $10.75 million was used to upgrade regional office spaces, focusing on creating more collaborative and flexible work environments. This included investments in new furniture, improved video conferencing capabilities, and enhanced cybersecurity infrastructure. This is in line with our commitment to employee well-being and attracting top talent. Software & Digitalization makes up 30% of Q3 2024 CapEx, or $34.5 million. This category represents a significant strategic shift, underscoring our commitment to digital transformation. A major investment ($15 million) was dedicated to the ongoing implementation of our new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system. This system will streamline operations, improve data visibility, and enhance decision-making across all departments. Full rollout is expected by Q2 2025. We allocated $12 million to accelerate our migration to cloud-based infrastructure. This will reduce our reliance on on-premise servers, improve scalability, and enhance data security. The migration includes moving legacy applications to the cloud and developing new cloud-native applications. We are partnering with leading cloud providers to ensure a smooth and secure transition. $7.5 million was invested in bolstering our cybersecurity infrastructure to protect against evolving cyber threats. This includes implementing advanced threat detection systems, enhancing data encryption protocols, and providing cybersecurity training to employees.

Now I’ll pass it to David Lee to provide color on execution.

David Lee, Chief Operating Officer:
Thanks, Sarah.

From a delivery and operations standpoint, this was one of our more efficient quarters in recent memory.

A big part of that was our operating margin performance, which allowed us to prioritize long-term growth and technological leadership, even at the expense of short-term profitability. The increased investments in R&D and the ramp-up of new manufacturing processes (7nm and GlobalTech 4) are crucial for maintaining competitiveness in the rapidly evolving semiconductor industry. However, the company needs to improve its execution, particularly in managing the costs associated with new technology ramps and mitigating the impact of unforeseen charges. Furthermore, GlobalTech must continue to diversify its revenue streams beyond traditional CPU sales, capitalizing on the growth opportunities in areas such as IoT, autonomous driving, and programmable solutions. The success of these initiatives will be critical to improving overall operating margins and delivering sustainable value to shareholders in the long run.

We also saw execution gains related to overall wafer ASP comments, including achieving a generally positive trend in overall wafer ASPs, driven by a confluence of factors, including increased demand in key sectors, a favorable product mix shift towards higher-value components, and strategic pricing initiatives. While we observed some softness in certain legacy nodes, the strength in leading-edge technology and specific market segments more than compensated, resulting in a net positive impact on our blended wafer ASP. We estimate that the overall blended wafer ASP across all nodes and segments increased by approximately 7% year-over-year. This growth is slightly lower than the 9% we projected in our last earnings call, primarily due to unforeseen fluctuations in foreign exchange rates and a temporary dip in demand in the European automotive sector. However, the overall trajectory remains positive, and we anticipate continued growth in the coming quarters. As previously noted, CCG Platform ASPs experienced a robust 15% increase year-over-year. This significant growth is primarily attributable to several key factors: We observed a strong shift towards higher-end laptops equipped with advanced processors and integrated graphics, particularly in the gaming and professional creator segments. For example, our "Spectra" series wafers designed for high-performance laptops saw a 22% ASP increase, driven by increased adoption of our advanced thermal management solutions and embedded AI capabilities. Units containing this wafer increased 18% Y/Y. The successful transition of a larger portion of our CCG portfolio to 7nm and 5nm process technologies significantly boosted ASPs. While the initial ramp-up costs associated with these nodes are higher, the enhanced performance and power efficiency they offer command a premium in the market. Specifically, our 7nm CCG wafers saw a 12% ASP increase, while 5nm wafers experienced a 8% increase in ASP compared to the previous quarter as production efficiencies improved. This increase in 7nm wafer ASP led to an increase in Q3 revenue year-over-year to $2.3 billion. Demand for premium CCG products was particularly strong in North America and Asia-Pacific (excluding China), where disposable incomes and technology adoption rates are higher. However, we saw slightly lower ASP growth in China due to increased competition from domestic chip manufacturers. We implemented targeted price increases on certain CCG wafers, particularly those with limited supply, to reflect the increased cost of raw materials and manufacturing capacity. These adjustments were carefully calibrated to minimize impact on overall demand while maximizing profitability. The Data Center Group exhibited a more moderate but still positive ASP trajectory. Platform ASPs were up 3% sequentially and 4% year-over-year. The introduction of our next-generation "Apex" server CPU wafers, featuring enhanced core counts and memory bandwidth, contributed to the sequential ASP increase. While the Apex series represents a significant performance leap, the initial adoption rate has been slightly slower than anticipated due to enterprise customers' rigorous testing and validation processes. We expect to see a more pronounced impact on ASPs in the coming quarters as adoption accelerates. We are increasingly focusing on optimizing our DCG wafers for specific workloads, such as AI, machine learning, and high-performance computing. These specialized wafers command a higher ASP due to their tailored design and enhanced capabilities. Our "Nova AI" accelerator wafer, for example, saw a 17% ASP increase, driven by strong demand from cloud service providers and research institutions. The integration of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) directly onto our DCG wafers is also contributing to ASP growth. HBM significantly improves memory performance, which is critical for data-intensive applications. However, the higher cost of HBM integration translates to a premium ASP. Lingering supply chain constraints, particularly in the availability of certain key components, have limited our ability to fully meet demand for DCG wafers. This supply-demand imbalance has put upward pressure on ASPs, but we are actively working to mitigate these constraints and increase production capacity. This lead to the company increasing the ASP for its "Titan" series wafers by 5% in order to counteract supply constraints. 5nm wafer ASPs remained strong, driven by high demand from both CCG and DCG sectors. 3nm wafer production is ramping up, and initial ASPs are significantly higher due to the complexity of the manufacturing process and the limited supply. We anticipate further increases in 3nm ASPs as we refine our manufacturing techniques and increase yields. Mature node ASPs experienced some downward pressure due to increased competition and declining demand in certain applications. However, we are actively diversifying our mature node portfolio by targeting niche markets with specialized requirements, such as automotive and industrial applications. Mid-range node ASPs remained relatively stable, with moderate growth in specific segments, such as IoT and consumer electronics.

Lastly, we began pilots tied to our sales guidance and forecast, where early signs are encouraging. As previously mentioned, our Q1 revenue is anticipated to be $18.3 billion. While this represents a 1% year-over-year decline compared to Q1 2021, it's crucial to contextualize this figure. In Q1 2021, we recognized a $600 million one-time corporate revenue item related to a significant licensing agreement. Adjusting for this anomaly, Q1 2022 revenue actually reflects a 2% increase year-over-year, signaling underlying strength in our core business segments. For the full year 2022, we are projecting revenue growth in the range of 4% to 6% compared to the adjusted 2021 baseline. This growth will be driven by a combination of factors, including continued momentum in our cloud services, strategic expansion in emerging markets, and successful execution of our product roadmap. Cloud Solutions remains our primary growth engine. We anticipate this segment to grow by 18% to 20% in 2022, fueled by strong demand for our integrated SaaS offerings and platform-as-a-service (PaaS) capabilities. Specifically, we expect our flagship cloud ERP suite, "Synergy Cloud," to achieve a 25% increase in new subscriptions, particularly within the mid-market segment. We also anticipate a strong performance from our AI-powered analytics platform, "Insight Cloud," driven by the increasing demand for data-driven decision-making. We project that CS will produce $3.8B in Q1 with a continued increase of 17% in Q2 to $4.4B. The Infrastructure & Security segment is undergoing a transformation, transitioning from traditional on-premise hardware to cloud-based security solutions and hybrid infrastructure offerings. While we expect some near-term headwinds due to the shift in revenue models, we are confident in the long-term growth potential of this segment. We are projecting a moderate growth of 2% to 4% for the full year 2022. This growth will be supported by the launch of our next-generation cybersecurity platform, "Sentinel X," which incorporates advanced threat detection and response capabilities. We anticipate particularly strong growth in our managed security services, driven by the increasing complexity of the threat landscape and the shortage of skilled cybersecurity professionals. Q1 is expected to generate $5.1B in revenue, with Q2 flat due to the ongoing shift in business model. This segment includes our legacy software applications and productivity tools. While we expect a gradual decline in revenue from our traditional on-premise applications, we are actively transitioning our customers to our cloud-based alternatives. We are projecting a revenue decline of 3% to 5% for the full year 2022. However, we anticipate strong growth in our cloud-based collaboration platform, "ConnectNow," driven by the increasing adoption of remote and hybrid work models. We are investing heavily in enhancing the functionality and integration capabilities of ConnectNow to make it the centerpiece of our digital workplace strategy. We expect Q1 to generate $5.5B. Our professional services division plays a crucial role in supporting our customers' digital transformation initiatives. We are projecting a growth of 6% to 8% for this segment in 2022, driven by strong demand for our consulting, implementation, and training services. We are particularly focused on expanding our expertise in areas such as cloud migration, cybersecurity, and data analytics. We expect a moderate increase in Q1 to $3.9B, and a more substantial increase in Q2 of 11% to $4.3B due to a few major projects planned for that quarter. We anticipate strong growth in Asia-Pacific (APAC), driven by the rapid adoption of cloud technologies and the increasing digitization of businesses. We are investing in expanding our sales and marketing presence in key APAC markets, such as China, India, and Southeast Asia. In North America, we expect continued growth in our core markets, supported by our strong partner ecosystem. In Europe, we are closely monitoring the macroeconomic environment and adjusting our strategies accordingly. We remain committed to our cloud-first strategy, focusing on delivering innovative cloud-based solutions that meet the evolving needs of our customers. We are investing in expanding our cloud infrastructure and enhancing the security and reliability of our cloud services. We are integrating artificial intelligence (AI) into our products and services to enhance their functionality and deliver greater value to our customers. We are particularly focused on leveraging AI to improve decision-making, automate tasks, and personalize customer experiences. We are actively building strategic partnerships with leading technology providers and industry experts to expand our reach and enhance our capabilities. aspect_summary.Operating margin results, QoQ changes, Y: Company-wide operating margin saw a slight contraction. Client Computing Group (CCG) operating margin decreased sequentially from 35% to 34% due to increased R&D spending and marketing, and decreased 3% year-over-year due to ASP pressure, increased R&D, and marketing spend, partially offset by reduced manufacturing costs. CCG's actual operating margin of 34% fell short of the previous guidance of 35.5% due to underestimated costs associated with 'Meteor Lake' and supply chain challenges. Data Center Group (DCG) operating margin decreased more significantly sequentially from 25% to 20.5% due to a one-time GlobalTech Federal-related charge and the 7nm product ramp. DCG's operating profit decreased 17% year-over-year. The actual result of 20.5% significantly missed the previous guidance of 24% due to an underestimation of the GlobalTech Federal-related charge and 7nm ramp costs.
aspect_summary.Revenue results, QoQ changes, YoY change: Q4 revenue reached $19.5 billion, exceeding the previous guidance of $18.3 billion by $1.2 billion. Full-year 2021 revenue was $74.7 billion, $1.2 billion above the projected $73.5 billion. Q4 revenue increased 7% compared to Q3 2021 ($18.2 billion) due to strong performance in DCSG and Notebook. Q4 2021 represents a 5% increase compared to Q4 2020 ($18.6 billion). Full-year revenue increased 2% compared to 2020 ($73.2 billion). The outperformance relative to guidance was primarily driven by strong enterprise and government data center demand, resilient desktop PC performance, and better-than-expected notebook demand.
aspect_summary.CapEx, and the CapEx comments for this q: Q3 2024 CapEx was $115 million, compared to $94 million in Q3 2023, a 22% increase. Equipment accounted for 45% ($51.75 million), space build-out 25% ($28.75 million), and software & digitalization 30% ($34.5 million). Equipment spending included upgrades to manufacturing facilities in Southeast Asia and data centers in North America. Space build-out was primarily for R&D facilities in Silicon Valley. Software & digitalization investments focused on ERP implementation, cloud migration, and cybersecurity. The company now projects total capital expenditures to be in the range of $28 billion to $30 billion, up from the previous guidance of $27 billion to $29 billion.

aspect_summary.government grants, local grants, tax inc: The company is pursuing government grants under the CHIPS Act, including potential funding for the Arizona expansion (Fab 53 & Fab 62) estimated at $3 billion to $5 billion, and the Ohio mega-site, potentially $9 billion in upfront funding. They are also seeking local grants and incentives in Arizona and Ohio, including property tax abatements, infrastructure improvements, and workforce training grants. aspect_summary.overall wafer ASP comments, and the by n: Overall blended wafer ASP increased approximately 7% year-over-year, slightly lower than the projected 9% due to forex fluctuations and a dip in European automotive demand. Data Center Group exhibited a more moderate but still positive ASP trajectory. Platform ASPs were up 3% sequentially and 4% year-over-year. 5nm wafer ASPs remained strong. 3nm wafer production is ramping up, and initial ASPs are significantly higher. Mature node ASPs experienced some downward pressure. Mid-range node ASPs remained relatively stable.
